description: Reviewed manifest for the Exercise II regression modelling table: the ABIDE-II FreeSurfer brain-feature table (Yarkoni NeuroHackademy tutorial) merged with the ABIDE-II phenotypic CSV. Single source of truth for scripts/abide_modeling_data.py, scripts/export_regression_catalog.py, the Exercise II notebook, and their tests. Change here, regenerate, re-test.

source.license: CC-BY-4.0 (repository LICENSE.md; the tu-machine-learning-yarkoni folder adds no separate licence)

brain_table.name: abide2.tsv
brain_table.note: 1004 participants, 1004 unique `subject` ids, no duplicates. Trailing empty header field is ignored. 6 non-brain columns + 1440 brain features. Zero missingness in the brain features.

phenotype_table.name: abide2_phenotypic.csv
phenotype_table.note: The same ABIDE-II phenotypic file Exercise I uses. Provides the cognitive / behavioural target columns that abide2.tsv lacks.

merge.note: Every one of the 1004 brain-table participants is present in the phenotypic file (0 unmatched). The merged modelling table is 1004 rows.

atlas.name: HCP-MMP1.0 (Glasser et al. 2016)
atlas.reference: Glasser MF, Coalson TS, Robinson EC, et al. A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex. Nature. 2016;536:171-178. doi:10.1038/nature18933
atlas.hemisphere_encoding: single letter L or R immediately after the measurement prefix
atlas.preprocessing_note: FreeSurfer-derived surface metrics summarised per HCP-MMP1 parcel. No further normalisation is applied in abide2.tsv; the notebook standardises features inside the training fold only.

5.note: WP14 audit (raw abide2.tsv, pinned commit e4eed3c4): this one HCP-MMP1 parietal parcel is the only ROI whose two hemisphere columns do not share a common raw suffix -- the left-hemisphere column is 'fs<measure>_L_5L_ROI' and the right-hemisphere column is 'fs<measure>_R_5R_ROI' (never 'fs<measure>_R_5L_ROI' or 'fs<measure>_L_5R_ROI', confirmed for all 4 measures, 1004/1004 participants, zero missing). Both columns are genuine continuous cortical measurements (e.g. CT range 1.30-3.42mm, matching every other parcel's plausible range), not identifiers, aggregates, or malformed fields. WP12/WP13 treated '5L' and '5R' as two separate single-hemisphere-only ROI labels and excluded both from the 'all-eligible' bundle, undercounting the canonical recipe at p=358 instead of 360. This entry corrects that: canonical ROI id '5' is genuinely bilateral like every other parcel, it is just labelled asymmetrically in this source table's column names.

age.label: Age at scan
age.meaning: Age at scan in years; a native column of abide2.tsv itself (no phenotypic-file join needed) and the Yarkoni tutorial's own target.
age.structural_note: Present for every one of the 1004 participants with usable brain data; 0 missing. Spans childhood through late adulthood (5.1-64.0 yr) across all 17 sites.
age.rationale: WP12 audit (scripts/regression_model_audit.py --run; book/config/regression_model_audit_result.json): age has reliably positive out-of-sample R2 with ordinary linear regression, unlike every FIQ configuration tested (all negative). WP12 5.4 policy: a target with reliably positive out-of-sample R2 becomes the main ordinary-linear-regression example. It also needs no join (available for all 1004 brain-table rows, not 908) and lets the leakage/scoring and sample-size sections use a signal that is actually there to lose to overfitting, rather than one that is not.

FIQ.label: Full-scale IQ (FIQ)
FIQ.meaning: Full-scale IQ (composite standard score; the exact test instrument varies by site and is not recorded per row in the merged 1004 - FIQ_TEST_TYPE is entirely empty here).
FIQ.structural_note: Present at 16 of 17 sites; missing entirely only at ABIDEII-EMC_1 (n=53). Balanced across diagnosis (autism 423, control 485).
FIQ.rationale: WP11 established FIQ is barely predictable from cortical morphometry in this sample (every tested feature set gives negative held-out/cross-validated R2 under ordinary least squares). WP12 keeps FIQ as a compact secondary example specifically to show, honestly, whether ridge or lasso regularisation can turn a broad brain-wide feature space from underdetermined-and-useless into something at or above zero -- see protocol.regularisation_preview. It is deliberately not the main worked example: WP12 5.4 says a target whose regularised score remains at or below zero must be reported as such, not promoted.

rejected_targets.VIQ: IQ subscale; FIQ is a composite of VIQ and PIQ, so pairing VIQ against FIQ is leakage-adjacent and pedagogically confusing.
rejected_targets.PIQ: IQ subscale; same reason as VIQ.
rejected_targets.ADOS_G_TOTAL: n=306 but ~87% autism group and near-absent at several sites (SDSU_1 0, OHSU_1 3, UCD_1 1, NYU_2 1); essentially confined to one diagnostic group and a handful of sites.
rejected_targets.ADI_R_SOCIAL_TOTAL_A: n=285, 0 controls; structurally an autism-only instrument, so a performance difference would be uninterpretable.
rejected_targets.SRS_TOTAL_RAW: WP11's lower-availability secondary target (n=764, both diagnostic groups, 13/17 sites) for a FIQ-vs-SRS availability contrast. That contrast no longer has a role once age (n=1004, 0 missing) is the main target and FIQ is the regularisation-preview secondary target (WP12 5.4/6.4); the WP12 audit did not re-test SRS_TOTAL_RAW as a candidate main target because it is a phenotype column requiring the same join as FIQ, with materially lower availability, and no literature framing distinct from FIQ. Still fetched by the merge (source.merge.phenotype_columns_kept) and available for a future exercise.

leakage_guard.principle: Every column of the model input matrix X must match atlas.column_pattern and name an ROI in roi_label_inventory. Nothing else may enter X.

protocol.preprocessing: sklearn Pipeline(StandardScaler(), LinearRegression()); the scaler is fitted on training rows / training folds only. No imputation is needed - the brain features have no missing values and rows missing the target are dropped before splitting.
protocol.generalisation_target: Held-out participants drawn from the same 17 ABIDE-II sites. A random participant split does NOT estimate generalisation to unseen scanners or sites.

canonical_recipe.note: Bilateral cortical thickness across every one of the 360 HCP-MMP1 cortical parcels (WP14 audit: all 360 raw columns per measure, confirmed genuine -- see atlas.hemisphere_specific_labels). Age-related cortical thinning is a whole-cortex phenomenon (Bethlehem et al. 2022; Storsve et al. 2014), not one a small literature-specified regional bundle would represent fairly, so the canonical recipe uses the full eligible ROI set for one measure rather than a hand-picked subset. p=360 stays well under n_train (~803 at the full holdout split, ~726 at 5-fold), so ordinary least squares is well posed.

regularisation_preview.purpose: WP12 6.1: a short, honest demonstration of what happens when p is comparable to or exceeds n_train, and whether ridge / lasso stabilise it, for BOTH targets.
regularisation_preview.note: p=1432 exceeds n_train at every split used in this manifest (holdout ~753-681, 5-fold ~803-726), so ordinary least squares is underdetermined for both age and FIQ here (diagnostic only, never the recommended model). Ridge and lasso are fitted with StandardScaler inside the pipeline and their alpha is chosen by an inner cross-validation on the training partition only - never by consulting held-out or outer-CV score.

sample_size_demo.purpose: WP15 sec 2: an isolated demonstration of what training-set size alone does to a fixed, modest linear model's held-out stability and accuracy, decoupled from the whole-cortex canonical recipe's own p=360 near-n=p instability (protocol.canonical_recipe; see the double-descent finding this recipe genuinely produces, documented unchanged in scripts/regression_model_audit_result.json / WPs/reports/WP14_REPORT.md and preserved in Exercise 2's main worked example, section 2-4).
sample_size_demo.note: sensorimotor_core was selected by a predeclared, training-only audit over 4 candidate compact (<=12-column) bilateral cortical-thickness bundles (sensorimotor_core, early_visual, auditory_core_belt, atlas_order_every_30th), scored ONLY against a fixed inner development split carved from the outer-training partition -- the locked outer test set (protocol.holdout_split) was never consulted while choosing the candidate. All 4 candidates passed the predeclared decision rule (clear upward median-R2 trend, materially narrowing instability, no interpolation-threshold collapse, seed-robust, meaningful final result); sensorimotor_core was the first passing candidate in declaration/source-preference order (a small, well-established literature bundle takes preference over the deterministic atlas-order rule), not the highest-scoring one. Full per-candidate audit table: scripts/sample_size_audit_result.json.

catalog.identifiability_rule: An entry is offered only if its feature count p is below 0.7 * (training n, from protocol.holdout_split). all-eligible x [CT,Area] (p=720) and any entry with p >= that bound is disabled with a visible reason rather than fitted with a pseudo-inverse.
catalog.note: The interactive feature-set comparison activity offers ordinary least squares only, never regularised models; that restriction is about this activity being unregularised OLS, not about p vs n in general (WP12 6.3) - the separate regularisation-preview computation (protocol.regularisation_preview) is where ridge / lasso are used, on the full p=1432 space, computed directly in the notebook rather than exposed as extra activity controls. Trying many entries here is still exploratory model comparison; the held-out score of the best-looking entry is not an unbiased estimate of its performance (WP19: every entry is scored once on the same fixed protocol.holdout_split test participants, not by cross-validation).

canonical_recipe.note: Identical to protocol.canonical_recipe (p=360), reused so this KNN result is directly comparable to Exercise 2's own OLS result: same participants, split, target, and feature set.

dev_split.note: Further splits the outer-TRAINING partition (753 rows) into a fitting subset (n_fit=564) and a validation subset (n_val=189) for the empirical all-k curve (Exercise 2 section 6) and the interactive activity (section 7). Independent of, and never touching, the outer test set (251 rows) locked by protocol.holdout_split.

knn.worked_example_k_rationale: WP19: k=20 is fixed by course design before the held-out result is computed, not selected by cross-validation -- early lessons no longer teach formal parameter selection. scripts/knn_model_audit.py --run confirms this recipe's locked held-out test R2=+0.664 (MSE 31.4) at k=20, evaluated exactly once -- higher than the two smaller predeclared bundles evaluated at the same fixed k (frontoparietal p=78: test R2=+0.465; occipital p=46: test R2=+0.425) and higher than Exercise 2's OLS result (R2=+0.469) on the identical participants/split/target/features. No curse-of-dimensionality problem is observed for standardized KNN on this canonical recipe, so the canonical feature set is retained (not a smaller bundle).

canonical_recipe.note: Identical to protocol.canonical_recipe and knn.canonical_recipe (p=360): Exercise 5 tunes and evaluates Ridge/Lasso on the same predictors as Exercises 2 and 4, not on the p=1432 regularisation_preview space -- feature selection and regularization are this exercise's own topic, not a repeat of the earlier p>n demonstration.

dev_split.note: Identical to knn.dev_split: splits the outer-TRAINING partition (753 rows) into a fitting subset (n_fit=564) and a validation subset (n_val=189), used for the 'Shrink the Coefficients' activity and Exercise 5 section 3's SelectKBest illustration. Independent of, and never touching, the outer test set (251 rows) locked by protocol.holdout_split.

regularization.grid_note: Audited empirically on the dev split (scripts/regularization_model_audit.py): with p=360 and n_fit=564, unregularised linear regression overfits sharply (validation R2 below 0) even though n_fit > p, because many cortical-thickness columns are highly redundant. Ridge's validation MSE is minimised near alpha~1e3 and Lasso's near alpha~0.1-0.3, both comfortably interior to these grids, not at either boundary.

nested_cv_pipeline.note: Identical outer/inner folds to Exercise 4 section 6's nested cross-validation, applied here to compare Linear Regression, Ridge, and Lasso (alpha tuned by inner GridSearchCV) on the full eligible cohort (n=1004) rather than a single train/validation/test split.

regularization.stepwise_note: SequentialFeatureSelector forward selection is demonstrated on the 'frontal' (prefrontal-only, 20 ROI, p=40 bilateral CT) bundle only -- small enough to run quickly and to show a readable selection order, unlike the full p=360 recipe.

canonical_recipe.note: Identical to protocol.canonical_recipe (p=360) and knn.canonical_recipe: the same 360 bilateral cortical-thickness parcels used throughout Exercise 2, so Exercise 3 needs no new feature-selection discussion.

holdout_split.note: Same test_size/random_state as protocol.holdout_split, but stratify is the diagnosis label y itself (group recoded to autism=1/control=0), not a covariate -- Exercise 3 is the first place `group` is the target rather than a stratification variable for a different outcome. This does NOT reproduce Exercise 2's 753/251 row split: the split target changed, so the partition is different even though test_size and random_state match.

classification.model: sklearn Pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=5000)); the scaler is fitted on training rows only. C is fixed by course design (WP19) before the held-out result is computed, not selected by cross-validation.
classification.worked_example_C_rationale: WP19: C=1.0 is fixed by course design -- early lessons no longer teach formal parameter selection. scripts/classification_model_audit.py --run confirms this recipe's locked held-out test accuracy=0.546, AUC=0.569, sensitivity=0.534, specificity=0.556, confusion matrix TN=75 FP=60 FN=54 TP=62, reproducing WP17's original untuned-C=1.0 result.

threshold_activity.note: Ships only the fixed honest test-set predicted probabilities and true labels (251 values each); the browser recomputes confusion matrix / accuracy / sensitivity / specificity / ROC / AUC at any chosen threshold from those two arrays -- it never refits the model.

imbalance_activity.cohort_size_rationale: WP17 sec 5: a fixed total N is drawn (without replacement, real participants) for every ratio so the demonstration only ever varies class balance and split strategy, never sample size. N=400 keeps every ratio's larger class within the available pool at 95:5 (380 of 541 available control participants) and every ratio's smaller class within the available pool at 50:50 (200 of 463 available autism participants), while making 95:5 meaningfully sparse: 20 minority (autism) participants total, about 15 in a stratified 75% train partition and about 5 in a stratified 25% test partition -- few enough to make the imbalance concrete, not so few that a stratified test partition becomes structurally impossible.
imbalance_activity.cohort_resample_note: For each ratio, the majority/minority participants are drawn once, without replacement, using random_state = cohort_resample_seed_base + ratio_index (0-5, in the ratios list order above) -- fixed per ratio, independent of the split seeds below, so every split seed for a given ratio compares the exact same cohort.
imbalance_activity.split_seeds_note: A predetermined selector for split-to-split variability only: each seed drives one stratified train_test_split(test_size=0.25, random_state=seed, stratify=y) of the same fixed per-ratio cohort, using the fixed C in classification.worked_example_C throughout. Stratification is an implementation detail here, not a separate comparison (WP18 sec 4).

canonical_recipe.note: Identical to protocol.canonical_recipe (p=360): the tree-complexity curve (section 3) and the fair model comparison (section 6) use the same predictors as Exercises 2, 4, and 5.

dev_split.note: Identical to knn.dev_split / regularization.dev_split: splits the outer-TRAINING partition (753 rows) into a fitting subset (n_fit=564) and a validation subset (n_val=189). The outer test set (251 rows, protocol.holdout_split) is never touched anywhere in this exercise.

single_tree.feature_selection_note: The two largest-magnitude training-partition (outer-training, 753 rows) correlates with age within the compact 5-ROI sensorimotor_core bundle -- not a search across the full 360-column recipe. fsCT_L_3a_ROI: r=-0.498; fsCT_R_2_ROI: r=-0.491.
single_tree.settings_note: The exact settings suggested by the course brief, audited and confirmed to produce a readable, non-degenerate 8-leaf tree on this feature pair (fit on the dev-split fitting partition, n_fit=564; evaluated on its validation partition, n_val=189).

complexity_curve.note: Fit on the dev-split fitting partition (n_fit=564, full p=360 recipe) and scored on its validation partition (n_val=189). Validation MSE is minimised at depth=2 and rises after depth=3, while training MSE keeps falling -- the section's overfitting illustration.

ensemble.random_forest_max_features_note: round(sqrt(360)) = 19, a commonly used default for randomized feature subsampling. An alternative candidate, p/3=120 (a textbook regression heuristic), was also audited (see scripts/export_tree_ensemble_widget.py); sqrt(p) was kept because it was decided before either candidate's validation outcome was compared, not selected afterward to manufacture a preferred result.
ensemble.note: Each of the 5 deterministic replicates draws 70% of the dev-split fitting partition (395 of 564 rows) without replacement at a predefined seed; every model in a replicate trains on the identical subset and is scored on the identical fixed validation partition (n_val=189). Bagging and Random Forest additionally perform their own internal bootstrap sampling.

fixed_prediction_replicate.note: WP30 sec 5: the 'One Tree or Many?' widget's observed-vs-predicted panel always uses this one fixed, predeclared training sample (the first replicate in the exported artifact) -- there is no student-visible replicate/seed selector. The distribution and ensemble-size panels still aggregate across all 5 replicate_seeds above.

fair_comparison.cohort: full eligible cohort (n=1004), not the outer holdout split
fair_comparison.note: Section 6's identical-fold comparison of DecisionTreeRegressor, BaggingRegressor, and RandomForestRegressor, all with the same fixed complexity settings declared above -- no hyperparameter search.

classification_complexity_curve.cv: StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) -- development rows only
classification_complexity_curve.note: WP30 sec 4, corrected by WP30R: a bounded, conditional audit of whether an autism classification tree usefully contrasts with the age-regression complexity curve above. Cohort, target coding, and feature recipe are identical to classification.canonical_recipe / classification.positive_class / classification.negative_class (Exercise 3): autism=1/control=0, all-eligible x CT (p=360). min_samples_leaf=5 is fixed by course design before viewing the curve, matching decision_tree.complexity_curve's own regression setting for consistency (not scanned for a favorable picture). WP30R correction: mean training/validation ROC AUC are computed by 5-fold stratified cross-validation restricted to classification.holdout_split's development partition only -- that exact outer train_test_split(test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=y) is reconstructed over the full eligible cohort, and the locked outer-test participants are excluded by row-level participant-set membership (asserted disjoint from, and complementary to, the development set) before any cross-validation fold is formed. WP30's original framing -- that the full-cohort version was fine because the script 'never read' a stored test-index object -- was incorrect: the full eligible cohort necessarily contained the outer-test participants, so their outcomes influenced every fold's AUC. Whether a second, classification-tree figure is added to the notebook is decided by a fixed rule (WP30 sec 4.2, unchanged), evaluated exactly once against this corrected configuration's result and not adjusted afterward -- see scripts/decision_tree_model_audit_result.json.classification_complexity_curve.inclusion_rule and WPs/reports/WP30R_REPORT.md for the actual outcome.

canonical_recipe.note: Identical to decision_tree.canonical_recipe / protocol.canonical_recipe (p=360): Exercise 7 reuses the same 360 cortical-thickness predictors as Exercises 2, 4, 5, and 6.

dev_split.note: Identical to decision_tree.dev_split / knn.dev_split / regularization.dev_split: splits the outer-TRAINING partition (753 rows) into a fitting subset (n_fit=564) and a validation subset (n_val=189). The parameter-explorer activity (section 4) and section 6's model-selection step both use this exact reconstruction; the outer test set (251 rows, protocol.holdout_split) is touched only once, in section 6 step 6.

sklearn_example.note: Section 3's short illustrative GradientBoostingRegressor example, fit on dev_split.fit and scored on dev_split.val. Not the tuned model used later; illustrates the API only.

step_by_step.formula: y = C + A*sin(FREQ*x) + B*x + noise, noise ~ Normal(0, NOISE_SD)
step_by_step.note: Entirely synthetic data (declared formula, fixed seed, decided before generation -- no seed search, unlike the Exercise 6 greedy-split activity, since no split-optimum 'niceness' criterion applies here). Not ABIDE observations. Stages 0..n_stages are precomputed for every learning rate in scripts/export_boosting_step_widget.py; stage 0 is always the training-target mean.

parameter_explorer.note: Precomputed grid for the 'Explore the Boosting Parameters' widget (scripts/export_boosting_parameter_widget.py) on dev_split.fit/dev_split.val only. Grid values were fixed before any model was fit -- not chosen after seeing which values created the neatest story. Uses sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor.staged_predict to obtain every displayed tree-count step from one fit per (learning_rate, depth) pair rather than refitting per tree count.

runtime_audit.measurement_note: Timed on the development machine with a same-shape (600x360) synthetic proxy matrix, fitting each candidate once per fold-equivalent and multiplying by 5 folds, before running the real audit -- not the audited run itself. Rule (declared before timing): if the full 27-candidate x 5-fold grid's audited runtime is disproportionate to every other exercise's audit (all under ~35s), reduce once to a predefined balanced subset of at least 12 candidates, never pruned by score.
runtime_audit.decision: reduced: the full grid measured ~357s (~6 minutes) for this one step alone versus ~10-35s for every other exercise's full audit; reduced to the 12-candidate grid below (~153s), fixed by structure (all 3 depths x 4 representative (learning_rate, n_estimators) pairs spanning low/mid/high cost), not by inspecting which combinations would be omitted.

cv_pipeline.selection_rule: minimum mean CV MSE across the reduced grid; ties broken by the earliest candidate in declaration order. The outer test set is never used to resolve ties or choose the grid.
cv_pipeline.comparison_cv: KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=100) on the full eligible cohort (n=1004) -- identical folds to decision_tree.fair_comparison, so section 7's table reuses decision_tree_model_audit_result.json's single_tree/random_forest numbers rather than retuning them.

recipe.note: Identical to gradient_boosting.canonical_recipe / decision_tree.canonical_recipe (p=360): Exercise 8 reuses the same 360 cortical-thickness predictors as Exercises 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7. PCA and K-means (sections 1-7) use the full 1004-participant eligible cohort; no target is required. Section 8 (PCA before KNN regression) reuses protocol.holdout_split for age, exactly as every other notebook.

unsupervised.standardization: sklearn StandardScaler. Sections 1-7 (unsupervised): fit once on the full 1004-participant cohort (no held-out split needed -- no target is predicted). Section 8 (supervised): the scaler is refit inside every cross-validation fold, never on the full development set before splitting.

loading_summary.note: Individual-ROI table: the n_top_rois strongest |loading| ROIs per shown component, signed. Grouped table: mean absolute loading (never a signed sum, which can cancel) within each of anatomical_groups, using the identical bundle ROI lists book/config/abide_modeling.json#bundles already defines and scripts/abide_modeling_data.py already expands -- audited for column-order consistency with the notebook's own natural-order 360-column FEATURES list.

projection_activity.note: Entirely synthetic 2-D data: mean-zero correlated Gaussian (sigma_x=3.0, sigma_y=2.0, rho=0.75), fixed seed, decided before generation. Sample-mean-centered so the stored cloud's own empirical mean is exactly (0, 0). Not ABIDE observations. The widget computes the projection onto the student's chosen angle, the captured variance, and the reconstruction MSE live in the browser from this fixed point cloud (pure closed-form trigonometry/linear algebra -- no model fitting, no Python runtime); the true PC1 angle and its explained-variance ratio are precomputed here for the reveal control and for the committed numeric audit.

kmeans_catalog.note: PCA is fit once (n_components=50, StandardScaler'd 360-feature cohort, random_state=0) on the full 1004-participant cohort; PC1/PC2 participant scores are the same for every retained_pc value because PCA components are nested (fitting with more retained components never changes earlier components' scores). K-means is refit for every (retained_pc, k, seed) combination in the grid above on the first retained_pc columns of that same score matrix -- never on PC1-PC2 alone, even though the scatter plot always shows only PC1-PC2. External variables (diagnosis, sex, site, age) are never inputs to PCA or K-means; they are joined onto the cluster labels only afterward, for display.

dev_split.note: protocol.holdout_split, reused unchanged; identical to gradient_boosting.dev_split / decision_tree.dev_split in spirit (same 0.25 test_size / group-stratification convention), but this is literally the single outer split shared by every ABIDE-II age-prediction notebook, not a separate one.

supervised_pipeline.cv_note: KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=13) restricted to the outer development partition (protocol.holdout_split), identical in spirit to gradient_boosting.cv_pipeline. StandardScaler and PCA are both inside the sklearn Pipeline and therefore inside every fold. Both n_components and k are selected together by minimum mean cross-validation MSE over component_grid x k_grid; the locked outer test set (n=251) is touched exactly once, after that joint selection.
supervised_pipeline.baseline_note: Comparison model: Pipeline(StandardScaler(), KNeighborsRegressor()) on the original 360 standardized features (no PCA step), with k selected from the identical k_grid under the identical CV folds. Neither model is guaranteed to win; the committed audit records the honest result.

recipe.note: Identical to unsupervised.recipe / gradient_boosting.canonical_recipe (p=360, n=1004, all with a non-null age): Exercise 9's ABIDE comparison (section 8) reuses the same participants, features, and target as every other exercise. The two interactive activities (PCR-or-PLS, SVM-boundary) use entirely synthetic, non-ABIDE data instead.

weak.label: Weak alignment with the highest-variance direction

moderate.label: Moderate alignment with the highest-variance direction

strong.label: Strong alignment with the highest-variance direction

pcr_pls_activity.note: Entirely synthetic, deterministic 2-D predictor cloud: two standardized, correlated (rho=0.7) features f1/f2, seed fixed before generation. In their own standardized PCA space, PC1 (direction (1,1)/sqrt(2)) explains 85% of predictor variance and PC2 (direction (1,-1)/sqrt(2)) explains 15%. The target is y = beta_pc1*PC1_score + beta_pc2*PC2_score + Gaussian noise(sd=noise_sd); the preset changes only (beta_pc1, beta_pc2), never the fixed predictor cloud or the fixed 40/20 train/validation split. PCR's component is chosen from PC1's own variance-only construction (never sees y); PLS's component is chosen using the covariance between the predictors and y.

svm_activity.linear_dataset_note: Two Gaussian blobs (mean-separated along one axis, shared covariance), linearly separable up to a small overlap.
svm_activity.nonlinear_dataset_note: Two concentric-ish classes (an inner class surrounded by an outer ring, plus noise) -- not linearly separable.
svm_activity.note: Two entirely synthetic, deterministic, fixed-split 2-D binary classification datasets (never ABIDE observations). Every (dataset, kernel, C, gamma) combination in the declared bounded grid is precomputed with scikit-learn's SVC; gamma is ignored (and its control disabled) for the linear kernel. Support vectors are always training-set indices; the stored decision grid is a fixed decision_grid_resolution x decision_grid_resolution mesh over a fixed, padded bounding box, sufficient for a smooth but compact Plotly contour.

outer_cv.note: Identical outer folds for every compared model; same (n_splits, random_state) convention as knn.nested cross-validation in Exercise 4.

inner_cv.note: Identical inner-fold assignments reused across every candidate of every model within a given outer fold, wherever a model has a hyperparameter to select; the standardized-OLS reference has none, so no inner loop applies to it.

rbf_svr.label: RBF SVR
rbf_svr.pipeline: StandardScaler() -> SVR(kernel='rbf', C, gamma, epsilon=1.0 fixed)

abide_comparison.gamma_grid_justification: For standardized 360-feature inputs (per-feature variance 1), sklearn's gamma='scale' equals 1/(n_features * X.var()) = 1/360 = 0.00278; the two numeric candidates (0.001, 0.01) bracket that value by roughly a factor of 2.8x below and 3.6x above.
abide_comparison.linear_svr_solver_note: WP34: measured directly on one real outer-training fold (n=803, p=360), a single SVR(kernel='linear', C=10) fit took 65s (libsvm's SMO solver); the full nested-CV grid needs roughly 800 such fits, an infeasible runtime. LinearSVR (liblinear coordinate descent) solves the identical epsilon-insensitive linear objective and is scikit-learn's own documented recommendation for this n/p regime; every fit completes in under 2s.
abide_comparison.linear_svr_grid_note: WP35: the WP34 audit found LinearSVR(C=10) did not converge within max_iter=5000, and remained non-convergent even at max_iter=100000 (an intrinsic conditioning property of this large-C, correlated-360-feature problem, not a solver artifact) -- while every outer fold selected C=0.1 regardless. C=10 was removed from the grid (now C in [0.01, 0.1, 1]). With C=10 gone, the new largest candidate (C=1) still needed more than 5000 iterations on real data (measured: up to ~8,924); max_iter was raised to 20000, at which every remaining (C, epsilon) pair converges cleanly (confirmed by direct per-fit timing, unlike C=10's genuine non-convergence). The audit was rerun; no LinearSVR convergence warning remains in the regenerated result.
abide_comparison.rbf_svr_epsilon_note: WP35: RBF SVR's epsilon (the width of the no-penalty band around each prediction) was previously left at scikit-learn's implicit default (0.1) and was not reported. It is now fixed explicitly at epsilon=1.0 (one year) for this teaching comparison and stated in the compact grid/parameter summary as fixed, not tuned -- only C and gamma are still tuned by inner cross-validation, to keep the teaching grid manageable. The full nested comparison was rerun after this change.
abide_comparison.note: Inner selection always uses mean inner-fold MSE (never R^2); every model is refit on the complete outer-training fold at its selected hyperparameter(s) and evaluated exactly once on that outer-test fold. No grid was adjusted after viewing any outer-fold result.

frontoparietal.label: Frontoparietal (P-FIT)
frontoparietal.literature: Jung & Haier (2007) Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory: dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (BA 9/45/46/47), inferior/superior parietal lobule and intraparietal sulcus (BA 7/39/40), and dorsal anterior cingulate (BA 32).

frontal.label: Prefrontal only
frontal.literature: The prefrontal component of P-FIT and of Narr et al. (2007): dorsolateral / inferior frontal cortex plus dorsal anterior cingulate, with no parietal ROIs.

parietal.label: Parietal only
parietal.literature: The parietal component of P-FIT: inferior parietal lobule (PG*, PF*), intraparietal sulcus (IP*, IPS1, LIP*, MIP, VIP, AIP) and superior parietal lobule (area 7 subdivisions).

temporal.label: Lateral temporal (comparison)
temporal.literature: Lateral / superior temporal cortex. Narr et al. (2007) reported some temporal thickness-IQ associations, so this is a scoped anatomical comparison, not a null region.

occipital.label: Occipital / early visual (comparison)
occipital.literature: Primary and extrastriate visual cortex. Not part of P-FIT's core; included as a similarly sized anatomical comparison bundle.

sensorimotor.label: Sensorimotor (comparison)
sensorimotor.literature: Primary and premotor / somatosensory cortex. A similarly sized non-association-cortex comparison bundle.

sensorimotor_core.label: Sensorimotor core (compact)
sensorimotor_core.literature: Primary motor cortex (BA4) plus primary somatosensory cortex (BA 3a/3b/1/2) -- the classic sensorimotor strip (Penfield & Rasmussen 1950 homunculus; HCP-MMP1 areas 4/3a/3b/1/2, Glasser et al. 2016). A minimal (p=10 columns), maximally well-established anatomical subset of the larger `sensorimotor` comparison bundle above, used only by protocol.sample_size_demo (WP15 sec 2) -- never by protocol.canonical_recipe or catalog, which keep the full 360-parcel recipe.

pfit.citation: Jung RE, Haier RJ. The Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory (P-FIT) of intelligence: converging neuroimaging evidence. Behav Brain Sci. 2007;30(2):135-154.

narr.citation: Narr KL, Woods RP, Thompson PM, et al. Relationships between IQ and regional cortical gray matter thickness in healthy adults. Cereb Cortex. 2007;17(9):2163-2171.
